messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for dedicated-pool-prod-us-west (SLO breach). Page: @oncall-engineering. Initial impact: streaming stalls, request queue growth. Link: https://redwood.ops/alerts/3033332222 :rotating_light:
sam: I'm on it, pulling metrics now. Seeing p95 ~ 350ms, p99 up to 2.4s, streaming stalls reported by a few customers as 'partial responses'.
aya: Confirmed queue depth jumped from 8 -> 62 on pool gp3-dedicated-usw. Warmup failures showing in logs.
jordan: Which autoscaler? Dedicated-autoscale-v2? Any recent deploys?
sam: autoscaler=v2, no deploys in last 30m. I see handshake timeouts between orchestrator and warmup workers.
lee: grabbing warmup logs from the warmup service. Suspect GPU allocation lag.
maya: support-alex, are we seeing customer tickets? Any high-visibility ones?
support-alex: Affected: 3 enterprise customers with degraded streaming. One open Sev 2 ticket, SLA threshold crossing. I told them we're investigating and will provide ETA.
ops-bot: Metric snapshot: pool_util=98%, queue_depth=59, warmup_fail_rate=12%, handshake_latency_p95=1.8s.
sam: Copy. Initial mitigation idea: enable temporary overflow routing to fallback lighter model on hosted pool for affected customers while we scale dedicated. Thoughts?
aya: That's reasonable for non-sensitive tenants. Can we route only streaming endpoints or full requests?
jordan: We can route text-gen and chat streaming to hosted-lite models but embeddings and regulated clients must stay in dedicated. Need per-tenant policy check.
lee: Warmup logs show GC spikes in the warmup controller and kube node pressure. Example error: ```ERROR warmup: failed to attach kv-cache: timeout waiting for slot (handshake 120s)```
maya: Do we have signal of node provisioning delay from cloud? Maybe instance launch throttling.
ops-bot: Cloud API errors: rate_limit_exceeded on instance create (x3) between ts 3033332180-3033332200.
sam: That explains autoscaler not getting capacity in time. So autoscale requests queued and warmup handshake blocking.
aya: Immediate actions: 1) Start manual scale-up of 6 hotshot workers in pool. 2) Bump handshake timeout to 180s temporarily to let slow nodes join. 3) Enable overflow routing for non-enterprise tenants.
jordan: I'll spin up manual instances (region us-west-2) and tag them hotshot=true to bypass rate limiter bucket. Starting now.
lee: Increasing handshake timeout config at runtime: ```PATCH /config/pool/dedicated/handshake_timeout = 180s``` Applying.
ops-bot: Config applied, handshake_timeout=180s.
sam: Routing rule change ready. Maya, deploy policy to route tenant groups alpha/beta/gamma to hosted-lite for streaming only. Leave enterprise_tier unchanged.
maya: Deployed route change. Confirming entries: ```match: tenant in [alpha,beta,gamma] -> route: hosted-lite (streaming=true)```
support-alex: Notified customers: message sent to affected tenants except enterprise ones. Will escalate enterprise ticket to account execs.
ops-bot: Manual instances creation started. 3/6 successful, 3 pending due to cloud throttling.
sam: After first 3 nodes joined, p99 dropped to ~900ms, queue depth down to 28. We still have tail stalls but improving.
aya: Warmup failure rate falling to 4%. Handshake latencies now 600-900ms.
jordan: Remaining 3 instances retried with increased backoff, now provisioning succeeded. Total added +6 nodes.
lee: Node pressure normalized. KV cache attach success logs: ```INFO warmup: kv-cache attached, ridge_id=rw-9987```
sam: p95 back to 180ms, p99 ~250ms. Streaming stalls cleared for non-enterprise tenants.
maya: Enterprise tenant still seeing intermittent stalls — looks like their requests are heavier and saturating model copies. Do we have capacity to spin additional copies pinned for them?
sam: We can add 2 dedicated hot copies for that tenant. Jordan can we carve out capacity?
jordan: Spinning 2 reserved copies (pin to nodes with hotshot=true). ETA ~90s.
ops-bot: Reserved copies ready. Enterprise p99 improved to ~430ms, streaming stable.
support-alex: Updated tickets. Enterprise customer responded: "thanks for fast mitigation, please follow up with root cause and long-term fix."
maya: Postmortem items: - autoscaler should have backoff-aware provisioning to avoid cloud rate limits - fallback routing policy for streaming should be automatic when handshake timeouts exceed threshold - improve visibility: add warmup_fail_rate alert targeting 5% over 5m -> page.
sam: Agreed. Also add autoscaler circuit breaker to detect repeated cloud rate_limit_exceeded and flip to manual-create mode.
aya: For now I'm leaving handshake_timeout=180s for 15m then revert. Also creating an incident doc with timeline and graphs.
lee: Logs for the period (snippet): ```[3033332170] cloudapi: create_instance failed: rate_limit_exceeded; [3033332199] warmup: attach timeout; [3033332228] node_join: success```
sam: Final status: mitigated, SLO still marked breached for window 3033332100-3033332300. Assigning postmortem to aya + jordan.
maya: Notifying pager rotation: @oncall-next, please review mitigation and accept postmortem.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated -> followup required. Incident owner: aya. SLA windows: breached (p99).
support-alex: Will follow up with customers and share remediation timeline.
sam: Thanks everyone. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours and then close thread if stable. :thumbsup:
